content: Veklury (remdesivir) is indicated for use in patients weighing at least 5 kg who are either hospitalized or not hospitalized but have mild-to-moderate COVID-19 and are at high risk of progressing to severe COVID-19, including hospitalization or death. It should only be administered in a hospital or healthcare setting capable of providing acute care comparable to inpatient hospital care. For children under 12 years of age or weighing less than 40 kg, the dose must be prepared using the lyophilized powder formulation, as per the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for this group. No dosage adjustment is required for patients aged 65 years or older. However, chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduce the effectiveness of remdesivir through an unspecified interaction mechanism. These drugs should be avoided or replaced with alternative therapies due to their interference with remdesivir’s intracellular metabolic activation and antiviral activity. Ublituximab may also reduce the effectiveness of remdesivir due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection; therefore, caution and monitoring are advised. Additionally, remdesivir may enhance the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism, necessitating careful monitoring. A pharmacokinetic study of remdesivir during pregnancy showed no clinically significant differences between pregnant and non-pregnant individuals, and no dose adjustments are recommended for pregnant patients receiving this drug. A published case report has detected remdesivir and its active metabolite (GS-441524) in human breast milk, but available pharmacovigilance data do not indicate adverse effects on breastfed infants. There is no data on the effects of remdesivir on milk production. For pediatric patients weighing between 5 kg and less than 40 kg, the dose must be prepared using only the lyophilized powder formulation. The concentrated solution (100 mg/20 mL or 5 mg/mL) should not be used in these patients or in those with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) below 30 mL/min due to the higher amount of sulfobutylether-beta-cyclodextrin sodium salt (SBECD) present, which results in increased tonicity compared to the lyophilized powder formulation. Remdesivir should not be administered simultaneously in an intravenous (IV) line with any other medication. The IV infusion should be administered over 30 to 120 minutes, and infusion rates may be adjusted based on the total volume infused. The formulation does not contain preservatives. For formulary comparisons, healthcare providers can create a list of plans to compare the formulary status of remdesivir with other drugs in the same class. This information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only, as individual plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. Providers should contact the applicable plan for the most current information.
